points.statement: The proposed generative-agent framework aims at cultural lifelong learning by making perspective taking explicit.
points.quote: We propose MindForge, a generative-agent framework for cultural lifelong learning through explicit perspective taking.

points.statement: The approach adds a structured percept-belief-desire-action representation, perspective taking over self and collaborator beliefs, natural-language information sharing, and distinct memory subsystems.
points.quote: To grant MindForge agents the ability to learn through collaborative social interactions, we introduce the following components for communication and perspective-taking: (i) an explicit structured representation linking percepts, beliefs, desires, and actions (Section 4.1), (ii) perspective taking so that the agent can reason over self-beliefs and those about its collaborators (Section 4.2), (iii) a communication medium that the agents can use to share information in natural language (Section 4.3), and (iv) the ability to utilize different types of memory subsystems (Section 4.4).

points.statement: Knowledge transfer is recast as a social inference-time process where agents update beliefs via multi-turn dialogue with expert peers and no gradient updates.
points.quote: Our framework reframes knowledge distillation [22] as a social, test-time process: agents refine their beliefs through multi-turn dialogue with expert peers, without gradient updates.

points.statement: The agent architecture adds causal perspective-taking over percepts and mental states, an inter-agent natural-language channel, and memory updates with semantic and episodic stores.
points.quote: Concretely, MindForge extends Voyager by incorporating three key improvements: (1) perspective-taking through a causal ToM template [17] linking agent percepts, beliefs, desires, and actions; (2) a natural language communication interface between agents; and (3) memory updates following the Soar cognitive architecture [34], including semantic memory of task and environment-related knowledge and episodic memory.

points.statement: The method contributes a structured mental-state representation, natural communication between agents, and a memory system with multiple components.
points.quote: We introduce three key innovations: (1) a structured theory of mind representation linking percepts, beliefs, desires, and actions; (2) natural inter-agent communication; and (3) a multi-component memory system.

points.statement: Interactive inference-time refinement enables agents to improve via communication, memory retrieval, and perspective taking.
points.quote: This interactive distillation supports test-time compute scaling [54], enabling agents to improve performance via communication, memory retrieval and perspective-taking.

points.statement: Organizing communication over multiple turns lets weaker open models match stronger ones through collaboration alone.
points.quote: By structuring communication across turns, MindForge also contributes to multi-turn LLM agent research [67, 13], showing that open models can match GPT-4 through collaboration alone.
